claims.text: Under the 2023 severely adverse scenario, the aggregate CET1 capital ratio of the 23 tested banks fell from an actual 12.4 percent in Q4 2022 to a projected minimum of 9.9 percent, then rose to a projected 10.5 percent at the end of the projection horizon.

citations.quotation:
Under the severely adverse scenario, the aggregate CET1 capital ratio of the 23 banks falls from
an actual 12.4 percent in the fourth quarter of 2022 to its minimum of 9.9 percent, before rising
to 10.5 percent at the end of the projection horizon (see table 1).

claims.text: Aggregate and individual bank post-stress CET1 ratios remained well above required minimum levels throughout the projection horizon.

citations.quotation:
The aggregate and individual bank post-stress
common equity tier 1 (CET1) capital ratios remain well above the required minimum levels
throughout the projection horizon.

counterarguments.text: Despite overall capital strength, banks with concentrations in mortgages, credit cards, and commercial real estate saw larger post-stress capital declines, indicating uneven resilience across the sector.

citations.quotation:
However, banks with concentrations in mortgages, credit cards, and
commercial real estate generally had larger declines in post-stress capital ratios this year.
